digest.component_or_area: LLM model class resolution for verification passes
propositions: Three separate code paths for verifier model selection use equality tests against DEFAULT_MODEL and silently revert to frontier model when the configured provider changes, breaking Bedrock cutover.

code-review.yaml's verify step declares no model: key, causing it to fall through to cfg.model (frontier) instead of resolving the standard class, and never applies its temperature: 0 determinism setting.

A single resolve_model_string() function in model_classes.py must replace three separate equality rules across verify.py, plan_review/__init__.py, and completion.py to eliminate split-brain verifier selection.

Workflow steps must express class selection by naming the class (e.g., model: standard) as a reserved value within the existing model-string space, which resolve_model() then resolves through load_class_slots() based on process-scoped configuration.

Provider-qualified model IDs (e.g., anthropic:claude-opus-4-8) bypass the equality rule DEFAULT_MODEL and leave the verifier on the frontier model even when the default provider changes, a defect the refactor must detect via cross-provider tests.

The verifier paths _verifier_cfg (plan_review xcheck callers), _verifier_model_for_completion, and code-review's verify step must all resolve the standard class regardless of cfg.model or provider qualification.
